• Status: Accepted (2026-10-14; concept v2 phase 8, ../concept-v2-scope-extension.md §B.2, decision 0.3)
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Related: ADR 0019 — TCP, BDX and the OTA Software Update Requestor (superseded in two points: the provider is no longer out, DiagnosticLogs no longer stays without BDX), ADR 0020 — the commissioner and controller role (the proof's counterpart), ADR 0011 — certifiability is a goal, notes/parity/by_design.md BD-Matter-OTAProvider-NotExposed, BD-chip-DiagLogs-NoBDX (both retire with this ADR's waves)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ADR 0019 brought BDX and the OTA requestor into the module and left the provider out ("another product") and DiagnosticLogs without BDX ("matter.js has none"). Concept v2 (2026-10-12, decision 0.3) reverses both for v1.0.0: a bridge that updates its bridged devices' firmware needs to serve images, and a bridge in a certification lab must hand its logs over BDX. The first read at the pin (0ceb202d, 2026-10-14) measured:

  • OTA provider in matter.js: OtaSoftwareUpdateProviderServer.ts (668 lines) is a full server: QueryImage with a software-update manager that validates the peer's BasicInformation and asks a consent and image source, Busy with a 2-minute retry (:218, :235), the BDX transfer offered as BdxSynchronous with a 5-minute idle timeout (:289-304), ApplyUpdateRequest answering Proceed or, without consent after 120 s, Discontinue (:248, :434-435), NotifyUpdateApplied. The BDX sender side exists in packages/protocol/src/bdx/ (OutboundFlow, DrivenSendingFlow, FollowingReceivingFlow — the receiver-driven transfer a requestor's ReceiveInit + BlockQuery opens; concept v2 B.2 named FollowingSendingFlow, which is the receiver's flow bdx/ already ports). The URI is bdx://<root node id, 16 hex>/ota/<file>, which bdx.FileDesignator.BdxURI already produces. The generated definition cluster/spec/otasoftwareupdateprovider and the device type OtaProvider (0x0014) exist; the type needs its own endpoint (BD-Matter-OTAProvider-NotExposed: on the root, Apple Home rejects the node).
  • DiagnosticLogs in matter.js: DiagnosticLogsServer.ts is an empty class — matter.js answers nothing. The premise of BD-chip-DiagLogs-NoBDX ("matter.js has no BDX transfer") was true but incomplete: it has no server at all, so chip is the only behaviour reference, as CLAUDE.md provides for what matter.js does not model. chip's diagnostic-logs-server (DiagnosticLogsCluster.cpp, BDXDiagnosticLogsProvider.cpp at the harness pin) is the BDX initiator and sender: on RetrieveLogsRequest(BDX, designator) the device opens an exchange on the command's session, sends SendInit, answers the command with Success after SendAccept, then streams 1024-byte blocks; Exhausted when the logs fit the response, Denied when the provider fails, InvalidCommand without a designator, ConstraintError above 32 characters, the oldest entry's timestamps in a Success response. The one DLOG case stays manual at the pinned image (an automated TC_DLOG_2_1.py exists only after the pin).
  • Two BDX roles are missing in bdx/: the responder-and-sender (the provider) and the initiator-and-sender (DiagnosticLogs); the messenger and the receiver flows exist. The bridge routes no BDX protocol messages inbound (bridge/receive.go: IM and SecureChannel only).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. The OTA Software Update Provider (0x0029) enters cluster/core as a port of OtaSoftwareUpdateProviderServer.ts with matter.js's defaults and statuses, and host ports for what matter.js's software-update manager decides: the image source (which image for a vendor/product/ version, as a file designator), user consent, and the apply policy. The BDX sender side is ported into bdx/ from matter.js's flows; the bridge routes inbound BDX to the registered responder. The provider lives on its own endpoint of device type OtaProvider (0x0014), assembled by the host; the reference daemon exposes one behind a TESTING-ONLY flag with a test image. BD-Matter-OTAProvider-NotExposed retires.
  2. DiagnosticLogs serves BDX as chip does: the server becomes a BDX initiator and sender on the requesting session, with chip's statuses and limits, cited line by line from diagnostic-logs-server; BD-chip-DiagLogs-NoBDX retires. The harness image pin does not move for this ADR; DLOG/2.1 stays a manual case.
  3. The proofs are in-repo and device-to-device, as ADR 0020's are: the module's own requestor downloads from the module's own provider (two node.Nodes on one fabric, commissioned by controller/client), and a DiagnosticLogs transfer is received by a BDX receiver on the controller side. The SU provider cases of chip (SU-3.x) are manual YAML; nothing built on this is described as certified (ADR 0011).
  4. Order: one wave (brief AQ): the BDX sender roles first, then the provider, then DiagnosticLogs; the reference daemon's provider endpoint last. Phase 9 (media) and ADR 0020 stage 6 are unaffected.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• docs/matterjs-comparison.md (the OTA and DiagnosticLogs rows), concept v1 §B.2's "provider out" line, ADR 0019's two points and docs/certifiability.md (the SU and DLOG families' notes) are updated by the wave's docs PR; CLAUDE.md's scope boundaries name neither and do not change.
  • The host's obligation grows by three ports (image source, consent, apply policy) and one endpoint; a host that wires none of them has no provider, as before.
  • Two by_design entries retire; the differences the port keeps (a Go file-backed image store instead of matter.js's DCL-aware manager, the pinned image's manual DLOG case) are recorded in notes/parity/ by the owner with the wave.

docs.title: ADR 0022 — The media and content clusters and the three media device types enter the scope
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted (2026-10-14; concept v2 phase 9, ../concept-v2-scope-extension.md §B.3, decision 0.2)
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Related: ADR 0013 — generated cluster definitions, ADR 0017 — the standard server (the mechanism that carries a generated definition with no logic), ADR 0018 — device layer, ADR 0011 — certifiability is a goal, concept v1 Appendix F.2 (the media family's exclusion, now lifted)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Concept v1 kept the media family out: fifteen clusters and three device types with no consumer in a bridge. Concept v2 (decision 0.2) takes them in before v1.0.0, generated, with the proof over chip's families and the module's own controller, because a bridge host may front a player or a content app and the parity count moves by fifteen clusters. The first read at the pin (0ceb202d, 2026-10-14) measured:

  • The fifteen (concept v1 Appendix F.2): MediaPlayback (0x0506), KeypadInput (0x0509), ContentLauncher (0x050A), ApplicationLauncher (0x050C), ApplicationBasic (0x050D), AccountLogin (0x050E), AudioOutput (0x050B), Channel (0x0504), TargetNavigator (0x0505), MediaInput (0x0507), LowPower (0x0508), WakeOnLan (0x0503), ContentControl (0x050F), ContentAppObserver (0x0510) and Messages (0x0097).
  • matter.js has logic for one of them. Fourteen servers are the generated extends XBehavior {} stub; LowPowerServer.ts:13-25 implements sleep() as an enterLowPowerMode event. The model (the element files) is the gold standard for the rest; there is no media example or test in matter.js at the pin.
  • The standard server carries fourteen. spec.NewServer (ADR 0017) mounts a generated definition with Source/Sink hooks and Server.Handle(cmdID, handler) for commands; an unhandled command answers UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND. It refuses a fabric-scoped attribute (cluster/spec/server.go:131-135, ErrFabricScoped): Messages' Messages attribute is R F V, so Messages needs a core-held server as Binding and EcosystemInformation have (device/device.go default factories). List- and struct-typed mandatory attributes have no rendered default: the host supplies the initial state.
  • Host ports are unavoidable for the commands that change state: MediaPlayback's transport commands, Channel, KeypadInput SendKey, TargetNavigator, MediaInput/AudioOutput Select*, ApplicationLauncher (whose StopApp also moves ApplicationBasic.Status on the content app's endpoint), ContentLauncher, AccountLogin (timed, fabric-scoped), ContentControl, ContentAppObserver, Messages, LowPower Sleep. WakeOnLan and ApplicationBasic are attribute-only.
  • Device types: BasicVideoPlayer (0x0028), CastingVideoPlayer (0x0023), ContentApp (0x0024), all revision 2, generated with no logic; the conditions PhysicalInputs, ContentAppPlatform and ObserverClient gate MediaInput, ApplicationLauncher and the ContentAppObserver client (wave 24 measured: on CastingVideoPlayer ContentAppPlatform gates the whole ApplicationLauncher cluster with the AP feature mandatory inside it; on ContentApp AP is disallowed). CastingVideoClient stays out (the client role).
  • chip's families: about 33 server-side YAML cases (ALOGIN, APBSC, APPLAUNCHER, APPOBSERVER, AUDIOOUTPUT, CHANNEL, CONTENTLAUNCHER, KEYPADINPUT, LOWPOWER, MEDIAINPUT, MEDIAPLAYBACK, TGTNAV, WAKEONLAN), hard-coded to endpoint 1 (3 for ALOGIN-12.1 and APBSC-9.1: a content app), user prompts automated under the image's CI PICS; the Python cases need PICS past the pin and skip. No CONCON or MESSAGES case.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. The fifteen definitions are generated (script/clustergen, cluster/spec/<name>), the fourteen without logic mounted by the standard server through one package, cluster/media, that wraps each in a typed host port (media.Playback, media.Channels, media.Keypad, …): the port is the interface a host implements, the server the generated definition plus the command handlers that call it and the attribute state the port reports. Messages gets a core-held server for its fabric-scoped list. LowPower's Sleep calls the host port, as matter.js emits its event.
  2. The three device types are generated (script/devicegen); their conditions are stated by the host as the root's are.
  3. The reference daemon exposes a player endpoint (a CastingVideoPlayer — chip's tv-app endpoint 1 is ma_casting_videoplayer, tv-app.matter:4384-4385, and the families need ContentLauncher and ApplicationLauncher there, which BasicVideoPlayer lists neither of; the first draft said BasicVideoPlayer — with a simulated transport, channel list, inputs and outputs) and a content-app endpoint (ContentApp with ApplicationBasic and AccountLogin) behind a TESTING-ONLY flag, driven by the app-pipe where a case needs a state change; the chip media families join the harness table, the PICS and the golden. The two Python cases that need PICS past the pin are recorded as not applicable.
  4. The ecosystem proof waits for phase 5 (Apple Home, Alexa with the owner at the device); nothing built on this is described as certified (ADR 0011). The parity count moves to 116 clusters and 77 device types, as concept v2's phase table says (measured after wave 24, #111: 118 served clusters — 115 generated definitions plus the three hand-written — and 79 generated device types, the OtaProvider and the 11 controller types of waves 21–23 included).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• docs/matterjs-comparison.md (the media row of the excluded families and the cluster count), concept v1 Appendix F.2 and docs/certifiability.md (the media families) are updated by the wave's docs PR; CLAUDE.md's scope boundaries name no media exclusion and do not change.
  • The host's obligation grows by the media ports; a host that wires none has no media endpoint, as before.
  • The concept's "all fifteen are stubs" is corrected to fourteen in the docs PR; defaultValue's missing list defaults are recorded in the findings register if the wave leaves them.

docs.title: ADR 0023 — Apache License 2.0 and a contributor licence agreement
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted (2026-10-15)
  • Date: 2026-10-15
  • Related: ADR 0011 — certifiability is a goal, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, CLA.md

docs.title: Context
docs.text: go-fabric was released under MIT (v0.2.0 to v0.4.0). It is a semantic port of matter.js, which is Apache-2.0, as is connectedhomeip; both chose Apache for its patent grant (§3), which matters in a protocol standardised by a consortium with patent pools. The owner weighed restricting commercial use (PolyForm Noncommercial, or AGPL with dual licensing) on 2026-10-15 and decided against it: the module's value is its upkeep and parity guards, not the code, which anyone can obtain from matter.js; the ecosystem proofs and certifiability (ADR 0011) need users more than control; a restriction would drop the module from pkg.go.dev's rendered docs and from any Home Assistant Core dependency list; and the released MIT versions cannot be withdrawn. What the owner wants to keep is the option to license the whole module under other terms later, which is lost the moment an outside contribution arrives without a rights grant.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Apache License 2.0 from the next release: LICENSE is the Apache text, NOTICE names the copyright and the matter.js lineage with its reproduced NOTICE, every Go file's SPDX header reads Apache-2.0, and TestLicenseHeaderOnEveryGoFile enforces it. Generated files carry the same header from their generators.
  2. The released MIT versions stay MIT. A licence already granted is not revoked; v0.4.0 and earlier remain available under MIT.
  3. A contributor licence agreement (CLA.md): every contribution grants the owner a copyright licence that allows sublicensing under any terms, a patent licence with a litigation termination clause, and the usual representations. Agreement is a line in the first pull request (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md); pull requests without it are not merged. Dependabot's changes are mechanical and carry no authorship.
  4. Dependencies stay permissive (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD): nothing in this decision opens the door to copyleft.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Apache-2.0 is MIT's superset for consumers: notices travel (NOTICE, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md), modified files need no change marks beyond the header, and the patent grant protects users of the Go code as it does users of matter.js.
  • Relicensing later stays possible for the whole module as long as every contribution came under the CLA.
  • CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md §Licence name the licence and the agreement; the changelog announces the change as a consumer-visible one.

docs.title: ADR 0024 — BLE commissioning in the controller role
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted (2026-10-16; concept v3, decision 0.1)
  • Date: 2026-10-16
  • Related: ADR 0020 — the commissioner and controller role, concept v3 §A.1, docs/matterjs-comparison.md (the BLE row and non-goal 2)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
"No Bluetooth" has been a scope boundary since concept v1: a LAN-attached bridge has no need to get network credentials onto a device that has none, and BLE pulls a platform radio stack into a library whose only other OS dependency is a UDP socket. Since ADR 0020 the module is also a commissioner, and a commissioner in the field meets exactly that device: a Wi-Fi or Thread product out of the box, whose only commissioning channel is BLE. controller/commissioner ports ControllerCommissioningFlow.ts without BLE, Wi-Fi or Thread (commissioner.go:83), so the reference controller pairs only devices that are already on the network.

matter.js at 0ceb202d carries BTP in packages/protocol/src/ble/ (BtpSessionHandler.ts, 875 lines with Ble.ts and BleConsts.ts), the advertisement in packages/protocol/src/advertisement/ble/, the platform in packages/nodejs-ble/ (2 092 lines over @stoprocent/noble), and the network steps in ControllerCommissioningFlow.ts:1527-1900 (addOrUpdateWiFiNetwork :1677, addOrUpdateThreadNetwork :1874). On Linux, BlueZ is reached over D-Bus without cgo (github.com/godbus/dbus/v5, BSD-2-Clause); CoreBluetooth and WinRT need cgo or COM.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. The controller role commissions over BLE; the device role stays without Bluetooth. A node of this module never advertises over BLE.
  2. BTP is pure Go in the main module (transport/btp), a port of BtpSessionHandler.ts proved against matter.js's test vectors; the seam controller/ble (Central, the advertisement parser, the PASE transport over a GATT channel) carries no dependency.
  3. The platform is a separate Go module, github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/ble/bluez, with its own go.mod: BlueZ over D-Bus, Linux only, no cgo. The main module keeps its five direct dependencies; a host without BLE never pulls godbus.
  4. The commissioner provisions the network after ControllerCommissioningFlow.ts: Wi-Fi credentials or a Thread operational dataset, ConnectNetwork, then operational discovery over DNS-SD and CASE. Provisioning a Thread dataset needs no Thread radio on this side, so "no Thread" (the node's radio) is untouched.
  5. Proof: BTP vectors; the network steps against the reference daemon with a simulated Wi-Fi driver (TESTING ONLY); end to end over virtual HCI controllers (btvirt) with connectedhomeip's all-clusters app in a manually started CI job; a real device in the manual test plan. Amended 2026-10-18 (owner decision, phase 13 report BB §3): the pinned CHIP image's apps carry no CHIPoBLE — --ble-controller exists only under CHIP_DEVICE_CONFIG_ENABLE_CHIPOBLE (examples/platform/linux/Options.cpp:170-172 at 6170af84) — so the virtual counterpart is a matter.js node with @matter/nodejs-ble (bleno on the second btvirt controller), the gold standard itself; connectedhomeip's app returns to the job when an image built with BLE is pinned. The job stays manually dispatched, on the ubuntu-24.04-arm runner: the x86-64 ubuntu-24.04 image's Azure kernel is built without Bluetooth (# CONFIG_BT is not set, run 39099608818), the arm64 one with CONFIG_BT=m and CONFIG_BT_HCIVHCI=m (probe run 39099728809). First green run 39101585016 (report BC).
  6. macOS and Windows stay out while they need cgo.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• CLAUDE.md's scope line and docs/matterjs-comparison.md (the BLE row, non-goal 2) name the device-side boundary and this ADR.
  • The sub-module has its own release tags (ble/bluez/vX.Y.Z) and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md; its version moves with the main module's.
  • BlueZ needs system-bus rights (the bluetooth group or a polkit rule); the reference controller's README says so, and the adapter's errors name the D-Bus cause.

docs.title: Getting started: the controller side
docs.text: The controller role pairs Matter nodes onto a fabric this module owns. It then reads, writes, invokes and subscribes on those nodes. It entered the module in stages under ADR 0020 and lives under controller/. This page builds the stack, pairs a node and uses it. The program is examples/quickstart-controller/main.go. The complete tool, with every command, is examples/reference-controller.

docs.title: The stack
docs.text:
A controller is assembled from the packages under controller/. The reference controller's openStack builds them in this order:

Step Package What it is Database store, controller/client/sqlstore the settings table and the client images; both schemas applied Certificate authority controller/ca the fabric's root of trust; issues our NOC and every node's Fabric controller/commissioner (NewFabric) our operational identity on the fabric Socket transport/udp, controller/exchange one UDP socket; sessions and exchanges with MRP DNS-SD controller/discovery the browser for commissionable and operational records Peers controller/peer the nodes of our fabrics, with CASE on demand Subscriptions controller/interaction the registry of client subscriptions Commissioner controller/commissioner (New) PASE, attestation, CSR, NOC, CommissioningComplete Registry controller/client one image per remote node, persisted

The quickstart's open follows the same order, and its close tears the stack down in reverse.

Source: examples/reference-controller/cli/stack.go:63-240, examples/quickstart-controller/main.go.

docs.title: The program
docs.text:
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 // Copyright (C) 2026 SukramJ.

// Command quickstart-controller is the smallest Matter controller on // go-fabric: it keeps one fabric in a SQLite file, pairs a node by its QR or // manual code, reads its NodeLabel, toggles its endpoint 1 OnOff and prints // the OnOff reports of a subscription until Ctrl-C. // docs/getting-started/controller.md walks through it; the reference // controller (examples/reference-controller) is the complete tool. package main

import ( "context" "crypto/rand" "database/sql" "encoding/binary" "errors" "flag" "fmt" "log/slog" "os" "os/signal" "syscall" "time"

_ "modernc.org/sqlite" // the host picks the SQLite driver

basicinfo "github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/cluster/spec/basicinformation"
onoffdef "github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/cluster/spec/onoff"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/controller/attestation"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/controller/ca"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/controller/client"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/controller/client/sqlstore"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/controller/commissioner"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/controller/discovery"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/controller/exchange"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/controller/interaction"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/controller/peer"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/im"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/secure/setup"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/store"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/transport/udp"

)

// openNames opens the DNS-SD cache; a test replaces it. var openNames = discovery.Open

// stack is the controller, in the order the reference controller's // openStack builds it. type stack struct { db sql.DB fabric commissioner.Fabric mgr exchange.Manager names discovery.Names peers peer.Set subs interaction.Subscriptions com commissioner.Commissioner reg client.Registry stop func() }

func main() { dbPath := flag.String("db", "quickstart-controller.db", "the SQLite file holding the fabric and the paired nodes") code := flag.String("code", "", "pair the node with this QR (MT:…) or manual code first") flag.Parse() ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM) err := run(ctx, dbPath, code) stop() if err != nil { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err) os.Exit(1) } }

func run(ctx context.Context, dbPath, code string) error { s, err := open(ctx, dbPath, "[::]:0", slog.Default()) if err != nil { return err } defer s.close(context.WithoutCancel(ctx)) if code != "" { if err := s.pair(ctx, code); err != nil { return err } } nodes := s.reg.Commissioned() if len(nodes) == 0 { return errors.New("no paired node: pass -code") } return use(ctx, nodes[0]) }

// open builds the stack over the database: the fabric (created on the first // run, loaded afterwards), the socket, DNS-SD, peers, commissioner, registry. func open(ctx context.Context, dbPath, listen string, log slog.Logger) (_ stack, err error) { s := &stack{stop: func() {}} defer func() { if err != nil { s.close(context.WithoutCancel(ctx)) } }() if s.db, err = sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+dbPath+"?pragma=foreign_keys(1)&_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)"); err != nil { return nil, err } if err := errors.Join(store.Apply(ctx, s.db), sqlstore.Apply(ctx, s.db)); err != nil { return nil, err } keep := ca.SettingStore{Settings: store.New(s.db)} // "controller.ca" and "controller.ca.fabric" authority, err := ca.New(ca.Config{Store: keep}) if err != nil { return nil, err } // A first run draws the fabric id and our node id; NewFabric saves them. fcfg := commissioner.FabricConfig{VendorID: 0xFFF1, Label: "quickstart", Store: keep, FabricID: max(random(), 1), RootNodeID: random()%0xFFFF_FFEF_FFFF_FFFF + 1} if , found, err := keep.LoadFabric(); err != nil { //nolint:contextcheck // the settings store's Load takes no context return nil, err } else if found { fcfg.FabricID, fcfg.RootNodeID = 0, 0 // the stored record decides } if s.fabric, err = commissioner.NewFabric(authority, fcfg); err != nil { return nil, err } l, err := udp.New(udp.Config{LocalAddr: listen}) if err != nil { return nil, err } if s.mgr, err = exchange.NewManager(l, exchange.Config{Logger: log}); err != nil { _ = l.Close() return nil, err } serveCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(ctx)) served := make(chan struct{}) go func() { defer close(served); _ = l.Serve(serveCtx, s.mgr.HandleDatagram) }() s.stop = func() { cancel(); <-served } if s.names, err = openNames(log); err != nil { return nil, err } resumption := &peer.MemoryResumptionStore{} fabrics := []*commissioner.Fabric{s.fabric} if s.peers, err = peer.NewSet(peer.Context{Exchanges: s.mgr, Names: s.names, Fabrics: s.fabric.Lookup, Resumption: resumption, Logger: log}); err != nil { return nil, err } s.subs = interaction.NewSubscriptions(interaction.SubscriptionsConfig{Logger: log}) //nolint:contextcheck // the constructors take no context; the peers they adopt resolve on their own if s.com, err = commissioner.New(commissioner.Context{ Exchanges: s.mgr, Peers: s.peers, Attestation: attestation.TestStore(), Logger: log, Subscriptions: s.subs, Fabrics: fabrics, Resumption: resumption, }); err != nil { return nil, err } s.reg, err = client.NewRegistry(client.RegistryConfig{ //nolint:contextcheck // as commissioner.New Store: sqlstore.New(s.db), Commissioner: s.com, Peers: s.peers, Exchanges: s.mgr, Fabrics: fabrics, Subscriptions: s.subs, Logger: log, Node: client.Config{Logger: log}, }) return s, err }

// close tears the stack down in reverse order. func (s *stack) close(ctx context.Context) { if s.reg != nil { _ = s.reg.Close(ctx) } if s.subs != nil { _ = s.subs.Close(ctx) } if s.com != nil { s.com.Close() } if s.peers != nil { s.peers.Close(ctx) } if s.mgr != nil { s.mgr.Close() } s.stop() if s.names != nil { _ = s.names.Close() } if s.db != nil { _ = s.db.Close() } }

// pair finds the device by the code's discriminator over DNS-SD and // commissions it: PASE, attestation against the CSA test PAAs, the NOC. func (s stack) pair(ctx context.Context, code string) error { var passcode uint32 var id discovery.Identifier if qr, err := setup.DecodeQRCode(code); err == nil { passcode, id = qr.Passcode, discovery.ByLongDiscriminator(qr.Discriminator) } else if m, err := setup.DecodeManualCode(code); err == nil { passcode, id = m.Passcode, discovery.ByShortDiscriminator(m.ShortDiscriminator) } else { return fmt.Errorf("-code: %w", err) } ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, time.Minute) defer cancel() sc := discovery.NewScanner(s.names) defer sc.Close() fctx, found := context.WithCancel(ctx) var dev discovery.Device _, _ = sc.FindCommissionable(fctx, id, func(d discovery.Device) { if dev == nil && len(d.Addresses) > 0 { dev = &d found() } }) found() if dev == nil { return errors.New("no commissionable device answered") } n, err := s.reg.ForDevice(ctx, *dev) if err != nil { return err } noSubscribe := false // this program exits; a resident host keeps the default subscription return s.reg.Commission(ctx, n, client.CommissionOptions{ Options: commissioner.Options{Passcode: passcode, OnAttestationFailure: attestation.Reject()}, AutoSubscribe: &noSubscribe, }) }

// use reads, invokes and subscribes through the node's client image. func use(ctx context.Context, n client.Node) error { label := im.ConcreteAttributePath{Endpoint: 0, Cluster: basicinfo.ClusterID, Attribute: basicinfo.AttrNodeLabel, HasEndpoint: true, HasCluster: true, HasAttribute: true} if , err := n.Read(ctx, client.ReadRequest{ReadRequest: interaction.ReadRequest{Attributes: []im.ConcreteAttributePath{label}}}); err != nil { return err } if ep := n.Endpoint(0); ep != nil && ep.Cluster(basicinfo.ClusterID) != nil { if v, err := ep.Cluster(basicinfo.ClusterID).Decoded(basicinfo.AttrNodeLabel); err == nil { fmt.Printf("NodeLabel: %v\n", v) } } toggle := im.ConcreteCommandPath{Endpoint: 1, Cluster: onoffdef.ClusterID, Command: onoffdef.CmdToggle, HasEndpoint: true, HasCluster: true, HasCommand: true} if , err := n.Invoke(ctx, toggle, onoffdef.ToggleRequest{}, interaction.InvokeOptions{}); err != nil { return err } onOff := im.ConcreteAttributePath{Endpoint: 1, Cluster: onoffdef.ClusterID, Attribute: onoffdef.AttrOnOff, HasEndpoint: true, HasCluster: true, HasAttribute: true} sub, err := n.Subscribe(ctx, interaction.SubscribeRequest{ Attributes: []im.ConcreteAttributePath{onOff}, MaxIntervalCeiling: interaction.Interval(time.Minute), Updated: func(r interaction.Report) { // keep it short: it runs on the report's exchange fmt.Printf("report: %d attribute(s)\n", len(r.Attributes)) }, }) if err != nil { return err } defer sub.Close() select { case <-ctx.Done(): case <-sub.Done(): } return nil }

func random() uint64 { var b [8]byte _, _ = rand.Read(b[:]) return binary.BigEndian.Uint64(b[:]) }

go run ./examples/quickstart-controller -code MT:-24J0AFN00KA0648G00
go run ./examples/quickstart-controller          # the same node, next run

The test opens the stack twice on one database and checks that the second run is the same fabric. It also checks that a malformed code is refused and that a valid code that no device answers ends at the deadline.

Source: examples/quickstart-controller/main_test.go.

docs.title: The fabric
docs.text:
ca.New with a store keeps the root key and the certificate counter. The CA saves after every certificate it issues, so serial numbers do not repeat after a restart. commissioner.NewFabric with a store loads the stored fabric record (fabric id, our node id, IPK, index, label, key and NOC). It mints and saves a new record only when the store has none.

A stored record wins over the configuration. A non-zero FabricID or RootNodeID that differs from the stored record is ErrFabricMismatch. That is why the quickstart sets both fields to zero once a record exists. ca.SettingStore keeps the CA under the settings key controller.ca and the fabric under controller.ca.fabric.

The database therefore holds the fabric's private keys. Anyone with the file controls every node paired to it.

Source: controller/ca/doc.go:4-17, controller/commissioner/fabric.go:21-58, controller/ca/persist.go:90-111, examples/reference-controller/README.md (The database).

docs.title: Pairing
docs.text:
1. Decode the code. setup.DecodeQRCode reads an MT: payload and gives the long discriminator. setup.DecodeManualCode reads 11 or 21 digits and gives the short discriminator. Both give the passcode.
  2. Find the device. discovery.NewScanner(names).FindCommissionable calls back for each device that matches the discriminator.
  3. Make a node. Registry.ForDevice returns the registry's node for the discovered device, creating one when needed.
  4. Commission. Registry.Commission runs PASE to the device's addresses, then the commissioning flow: ArmFailSafe, device attestation, CSR, NOC, the operational CASE connection, and CommissioningComplete. The record and settings are saved, and the node starts.

CommissionOptions decides the rest:

  • NodeID: 0 draws a random operational node id that no peer of the fabric has.
  • AutoSubscribe: nil or true keeps the node live through one sustained wildcard subscription. The quickstart turns it off because it exits.
  • NoInitialRead: skips the initial read after commissioning.

A second Commission of a commissioned node is ErrAlreadyCommissioned. A commission or decommission already running for that node is ErrFabricOperationInProgress. Registry.Decommission sends RemoveFabric to the node and then deletes it. If the node refused the removal, or the removal was not confirmed, Decommission returns that error and keeps the node.

A Wi-Fi or Thread device out of the box is found over BLE instead (ADR 0024): ble.NewScanner(central).Find matches its advertisement by the same discriminator, ble.Dial opens the BTP channel, and Registry.Commission with Options.Channel runs PASE over it, then the network steps with Options.WiFiNetwork or ThreadNetwork; operational discovery finds the device over DNS-SD for CASE. The central on Linux is github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/ble/bluez, a module of its own so the main module never pulls its D-Bus dependency; the reference controller's BLE build is its cmd/reference-controller (pair --ble, rights and BlueZ version in the reference controller's README).

Source: examples/reference-controller/cli/pair.go:37-189, examples/reference-controller/cli/pair.go:214-246, ble/bluez/doc.go:4-30, controller/client/fabricops.go:108-157, controller/client/fabricops.go:224-232, controller/commissioner/commissioner.go:85-123, controller/commissioner/doc.go:4-19, controller/client/registry.go:176-191.

docs.title: Attestation and the DCL
docs.text:
The commissioner checks the device's attestation against a trust store:

  • attestation.TestStore() (the quickstart's choice) holds the CSA test PAAs and the test CD signer. It accepts the test devices that the reference bridge and chip-tool present.
  • A nil store checks without one, as matter.js does without its DCL service.
  • dcl.OpenCertificateStore is the opt-in trust store from the CSA Distributed Compliance Ledger. Nothing in controller/dcl reaches the network unless you construct a dcl.Client and hand it over. The ledger then learns the key identifiers of the PAAs, PAIs and CD signers of the devices you attest; no device identity, passcode or fabric key is sent.

The policy decides what a finding does:

Policy Effect on a finding attestation.Accept() proceeds; each finding is logged attestation.Reject() rejects the commissioning Policy{Decide: …} your function decides alone zero value Policy{} proceeds, with a warning per finding

The zero value proceeds because matter.js does the same for backward compatibility. Set the policy explicitly.

Source: controller/attestation/doc.go:4-20, controller/attestation/store.go:87-93, controller/attestation/policy.go:17-61, controller/commissioner/commissioner.go:52-54, controller/dcl/doc.go:4-24, examples/reference-controller/cli/stack.go:242-297.

docs.title: The registry and the device view
docs.text:
The client.Registry restores every node its store holds when it is built. Registry.Start starts the commissioned, enabled nodes only when RegistryConfig.AutoStart is set. Use these calls to find a node:

Call Returns Get(id) the node with a local id (peer1, peer2, …) GetByAddress(fabric.AddressOf(nodeID)) the node with a node id Commissioned() every commissioned node

A client.Node is the controller's image of the remote node. The controller has no device model of its own: the remote node's Descriptor decides the endpoints and the generated cluster definitions decide each cluster's shape.

Call Returns Endpoints(), Endpoint(n) the image's endpoints Endpoint.DeviceType(), Endpoint.Device() the device type id, and its definition when known Endpoint.Clusters(), Endpoint.Cluster(id) the clusters Cluster.Decoded(attr) an attribute value, decoded through the definition Cluster.Value(attr) the raw TLV tree

The image is persisted with controller/client/sqlstore, so a later run starts from what the last one saw.

Source: controller/client/doc.go:19-50, controller/client/registry.go:24-191, controller/client/registry.go:343-369, controller/client/endpoint.go:53-145, controller/client/cluster.go:204-345, examples/reference-controller/cli/pair.go:191-212.

docs.title: Read, write, invoke, subscribe
docs.text:
All four go through the node and its CASE session. The peer set establishes CASE when no session is live.

  • Read. Node.Read applies the report to the image and returns it. Unless IncludeKnownVersions is set, the cached data versions go along as filters, so the peer sends only clusters that changed.
  • Write. Node.Write takes interaction.WriteRequests, each a path and a value. The value is a generated type, or a TLV tree through interaction.Raw. DataVersion makes a write conditional. The write goes to the peer only, and the image follows when the peer reports the new value.
  • Invoke. Node.Invoke takes the command path and the generated request type (onoffdef.ToggleRequest{}). InvokeOptions{Timed: true} sends a TimedRequest first.
  • Subscribe. Node.Subscribe applies each report to the image before Updated sees it. Updated runs on the goroutine that reads the report, inside the report's exchange, so keep it short. The reference controller hands each report to a channel. Sustain re-establishes a subscription that was lost.

Source: controller/client/interact.go:15-120, controller/interaction/write.go:39-52, controller/interaction/invoke.go:19-31, controller/interaction/subscribe.go:44-90, controller/interaction/handler.go:126-138, examples/reference-controller/cli/interact.go:289-330.

docs.title: What is not here yet
docs.text:
BLE on macOS and Windows (ADR 0024 decision 6) and TCP on the controller side are outside the current stages. Group messages and OTA images need a node of the fabric. The reference controller starts its own node for group and ota and keeps it in the same database.

Source: controller/commissioner/doc.go:15-19, controller/peer/doc.go:12-16, examples/reference-controller/README.md (The controller's own node).

docs.title: Getting started: the device side
docs.text: This page builds a Matter bridge with one on/off light, pairs it, and walks through what each part of the program does. The program is examples/quickstart-device/main.go; its test builds it, starts the node on loopback, stops it and starts it again on the same database.

docs.title: node/ or bridge/?
docs.text:
Embed node/ unless you have a reason not to. node.New performs the whole bring-up the reference daemon used to do by hand: the stores, the root and Aggregator endpoints, PASE and CASE, the subscription engine, the commissioning window, the fabric hooks, and every port of bridge/ in its documented order. You configure it with one node.Config and add devices to its Aggregator.

Use the facade with your own topology when you already have an endpoint assembler over your own device model: set Config.Topology to your bridge.Snapshotter. The facade then builds no Aggregator, and everything else (stores, root servers, sessions, group state) stays the facade's.

Use bridge/ directly only if you need to replace one of the collaborators the facade wires. bridge.New installs a no-op for every port you do not attach, so a half-wired bridge binds its socket, publishes mDNS and answers datagrams wrongly. The ports guide lists every port, what skipping it costs, and whether the failure is visible. Node.Bridge() gives you the bridge for a port the facade does not cover without leaving the facade.

Source: node/doc.go:4-43, node/config.go:94-103, bridge/bridge.go:29-47, node/node.go:601-603.

docs.title: The program
docs.text:
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 // Copyright (C) 2026 SukramJ.

// Command quickstart-device is the smallest Matter bridge on go-fabric: one // on/off light under the node's Aggregator, its state in one SQLite file, // advertised over DNS-SD. docs/getting-started/device.md walks through it. // It pairs with the CSA test identity and is not a product. package main

import ( "context" "database/sql" "fmt" "log/slog" "os" "os/signal" "slices" "syscall"

_ "modernc.org/sqlite" // the host picks the SQLite driver

"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/cluster/onoff"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/device"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/endpoint"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/mdns"
"github.com/SukramJ/go-fabric/node"

)

func main() { ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM) err := run(ctx) stop() if err != nil { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err) os.Exit(1) } }

func run(ctx context.Context) error { db, err := openDB("quickstart-device.db") if err != nil { return err } defer func() { _ = db.Close() }()

// DNS-SD: the subtype responder answers the discriminator-filtered
// browse every commissioner sends for a QR or manual code.
zc := mdns.NewZeroconf()
if r, err := mdns.NewSubtypeResponder(slog.Default()); err == nil {
    r.Start(ctx)
    zc.AttachSubtypeResponder(r)
    defer func() { _ = r.Close() }()
}

n, err := newNode(ctx, db, node.Network{}, zc)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
qr, manual, err := n.PairingCodes()
if err != nil {
    _ = n.Stop(context.WithoutCancel(ctx))
    return err
}
fmt.Printf("QR code: %s\nManual code: %s\n", qr, manual)
return n.Run(ctx) // Start, wait for ctx, Stop

}

// openDB opens the SQLite file; foreign_keys carries the store's // cascade-delete on fabric removal. node.New applies the schemas. func openDB(path string) (*sql.DB, error) { return sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+path+"?_pragma=foreign_keys(1)&_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)") }

// newNode builds the node and adds the light, unstarted. func newNode(ctx context.Context, db sql.DB, network node.Network, adv mdns.Advertiser) (node.Node, error) { n, err := node.New(node.Config{ //nolint:contextcheck // the node's constructor takes no context Network: network, Commissioning: node.Commissioning{ // change all four for anything real Passcode: 20202021, Discriminator: 3840, PBKDFIterations: 1000, Salt: []byte("go-fabric-quickstart"), }, ProductDescription: node.ProductDescription{VendorID: 0xFFF1, ProductID: 0x8001}, // CSA test vendor BasicInformation: node.BasicInformation{ VendorName: "quickstart", ProductName: "quickstart-device", NodeLabel: "Quickstart bridge", SerialNumber: "QUICKSTART-0001", }, Store: node.Store{DB: db}, Advertiser: adv, }) if err != nil { return nil, err } light, err := device.NewOnOffLight(device.Options{StableKey: endpoint.StringKey("light-1"), Name: "Desk lamp"}) if err == nil { light.OnChanged(onoff.ClusterID, func(attrs []uint32) { if slices.Contains(attrs, onoff.AttrOnOff) { slog.Info("light", slog.Bool("on", light.OnOff().OnOff())) // drive the real lamp here } }) err = n.Aggregator().Add(ctx, light) } if err != nil { _ = n.Stop(context.WithoutCancel(ctx)) return nil, err } n.Aggregator().MarkComplete() //nolint:contextcheck // the node's own; every device is added: stale endpoint numbers may go return n, nil }

Run it, scan the QR code or enter the manual code in a commissioner, and the light appears under the bridge:

go run ./examples/quickstart-device

It listens on UDP port 5540 and needs IPv6 and multicast on the LAN, like any Matter device. A commissioner that filters by discriminator, which is what Apple Home, Google Home and chip-tool do for a QR or manual code, finds the device only through the subtype responder. Without the responder, _matterc._udp lists the instance, but the discriminator subtype query gets no answer.

Source: examples/quickstart-device/main.go, examples/quickstart-device/main_test.go, examples/reference-bridge/main.go:178-201, node/config.go:144-145.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
node.New calls Config.Validate first and refuses the whole configuration with node.ErrInvalidConfig when any check fails. It checks:

  • the discriminator fits 12 bits;
  • the passcode is in range and not on the trivially-guessable list;
  • the PBKDF iteration count and salt length are what SPAKE2+ accepts;
  • VendorID, ProductID and NodeLabel are set;
  • a store is given (see below);
  • SupportedFabrics is at most 254;
  • UniqueID is at most 32 bytes;
  • LocationCapability is a valid regulatory location;
  • Network.ReannounceInterval is not negative;
  • OTA.Dir is set when OTA is.

The quickstart uses the CSA test vendor 0xFFF1. With no Attestation set, the node serves the CSA test attestation chain and test Certification Declaration for the configured vendor and product. Every commissioner accepts that chain through its test PAA, and a product must not ship with it. A product sets Config.Attestation to its own DAC, PAI and CD.

Defaults worth knowing:

Field Zero value means Network.Listen :5540 Advertiser mdns.NewNoop(): nothing is published, so nothing can discover the node DeviceTypeValidation matter.js's warn mode SupportedFabrics 5 (matter.js defaults to 254) ProductDescription.Name BasicInformation.NodeLabel ProductDescription.DeviceType RootNode (0x0016) BasicInformation.UniqueID derived on the first boot and pinned in the store Locales en-US alone Logger slog.Default()

Source: node/config.go:28-139, node/config.go:215-279, node/config.go:333-381, node/node.go:109-120.

docs.title: Devices
docs.text:
The device/ package has one constructor per Matter device type in scope: device.NewOnOffLight, device.NewDimmableLight, device.NewThermostat and so on. They are generated from the matter.js model. A constructor mounts every server cluster the device type mandates, with a default server (the module's own where one exists, otherwise the generated spec.Server). The endpoint assembler mounts Descriptor, Identify, BridgedDeviceBasicInformation, Groups and ScenesManagement; the device layer never does.

device.Options identifies the device:

  • StableKey is required and unique. The assembler keeps the endpoint number under it, so the same key gets the same endpoint number after a restart. The quickstart's test checks this.
  • Name becomes the bridged device's NodeLabel. Vendor is its manufacturer.
  • Reachable is a probe for the device's reachability; nil means always reachable.

Options passed after Options change what the device serves:

Option Effect WithServer(srv) your own server for a cluster, replacing the default WithOptional(id) mounts an optional cluster (Groups and ScenesManagement are then the assembler's) WithFeatures(id, bits) the features of a cluster's default server WithElements(id, opts) optional attributes, commands and events of a default server WithInitial(id, values) initial attribute values of a default server WithMeasurement(src) a sensor's measurement clusters from your live reading WithChangeNotifier(n) tells the bridge your model changed state its servers read WithClientClusters(ids...) client clusters beyond the mandatory ones

docs.title: Two directions of state
docs.text:
A device's state moves both ways, and the two directions use different calls:

  • Controller to device. Device.OnChanged(clusterID, fn) calls fn with the attribute ids that changed. The quickstart uses it to log the light's new state. To refuse a command, for example when the physical lamp did not switch, give the light your own onoff.Server with a Sink (onoff.Config.Sink through WithServer). An error from the sink answers FAILURE and stores nothing.
  • Device to controller. When the lamp is switched at the wall, call light.OnOff().Set(on). The value is stored and reported to subscribers, and the sink is not called. Set is safe from any goroutine, including from inside the sink.

Source: device/doc.go:4-27, device/options.go:18-43, device/options.go:91-215, device/device.go:643-661, cluster/onoff/server.go:54-72, cluster/onoff/server.go:749-768.

docs.title: The Aggregator
docs.text:
Node.Aggregator() is the Aggregator endpoint's set of bridged devices.

  • Before Start, Add and Remove only change the set. The first assembly happens at Start.
  • After Start, each Add and Remove reassembles the running bridge.
  • An endpoint without a StableKey is refused with ErrNoStableKey. A second endpoint with the same key is refused with ErrDuplicateKey.

Call MarkComplete once every device you know about is added. Until then the node keeps the stored endpoint numbers of devices that are absent. Afterwards, a stored device missing from the set loses its number. A host whose model loads asynchronously calls MarkComplete after the load. If it is called too early, the endpoint numbers of devices not yet loaded are garbage-collected at boot, and every controller sees those devices as new.

Source: node/aggregator.go:40-132, examples/reference-bridge/main.go:328-332.

docs.title: Commissioning
docs.text:
Node.PairingCodes returns the QR payload and the 11-digit manual code for the configured passcode and discriminator. When Start loads no fabric from the store, it opens the node's own commissioning window. A commissioned node opens a window only when a controller asks for one through AdministratorCommissioning, or when you call Node.OpenBasicWindow with fresh credentials.

Node.SetCommissioningBlocked(ctx, err) refuses every new commissioning while err is non-nil, and controllers that are already paired keep working. A host calls it before Start when, for example, it cannot serve its configured attestation chain.

Source: node/node.go:691-712, node/node.go:526-534, node/commissioning.go:426-454, node/node.go:641-662.

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:
Config.Store.DB is a *sql.DB that you open; no library package imports a SQLite driver. The quickstart uses modernc.org/sqlite, the pure-Go driver the module already depends on. node.New applies both schemas (fabrics, credentials, ACL, groups, subscriptions, settings, and endpoint numbers) to that handle on every boot; both scripts are idempotent.

Open the database with _pragma=foreign_keys(1) in the DSN. The fabric tables cascade-delete through foreign keys, and SQLite ignores those silently with the pragma off. The pragma must be in the DSN, not in a statement, so that every pooled connection gets it.

The persistence guide lists every table and settings key.

Source: node/config.go:281-290, node/node.go:300-317, examples/reference-bridge/persist.go:24-34.

docs.title: Stopping
docs.text:
Node.Run(ctx) starts the node, waits for ctx to end, and stops it with a 5-second budget. Node.Stop runs the shutdown in a fixed order:

  1. the OTA requestor stops;
  2. the operational time is stored and the ShutDown event is emitted;
  3. the bindings and client stack close;
  4. PASE, the commissioning window and the CASE reaper stop;
  5. the subscription engine, the group sender, BDX and the re-announce loop stop;
  6. the bridge stops (sessions are closed with a CloseSession to each peer, then the socket closes and the mDNS records are withdrawn);
  7. the advertiser closes.

Stop is idempotent and safe without Start. A stopped node does not restart: Start after Stop returns node.ErrStopped. To restart, build a new node on the same store.

New already starts the subscription engine and the session reapers. Call Stop on every node that New returned, including one you never started. The quickstart does this on its error paths.

Source: node/node.go:34-36, node/node.go:538-599, node/node.go:95-108, bridge/bridge.go:1541-1556.

docs.title: What the reference daemon adds
docs.text:
examples/reference-bridge is the facade plus the host's own pieces, each of which is something a product would also decide:

  • Flags for the listen address, TCP, passcode, discriminator, PBKDF parameters, label and log level. Each flag is checked before the node is built.
  • A vendor attestation chain read from a directory instead of the test chain.
  • The OTA requestor with an applier that validates and keeps the image. This is the host's OtaApplier.
  • An Actions server on the Aggregator, root FixedLabels and two locales.
  • A fleet of simulated devices, one per surface the module serves. The blind's position is persisted in the settings table.
  • Testing-only flags for certification runs: the app pipe, the TestEventTrigger key, the OTA provider and its ledger check, the simulated Wi-Fi link and the media devices. None of these belongs in a product.

Source: examples/reference-bridge/main.go:4-24, examples/reference-bridge/main.go:96-145, examples/reference-bridge/main.go:147-299, examples/reference-bridge/main.go:306-391, examples/reference-bridge/persist.go:68-86.

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text: The module is concurrent by construction: a host's cluster servers are called from many goroutines at once, and the session, subscription and MRP paths run side by side. This page lists the goroutines a running node owns, what a host callback may do, the ordering the module guarantees, and how shutdown ends it all. The race detector run (make race) is a release gate for these paths.

docs.title: The goroutines of a running node
docs.text:
Goroutine Started by Cadence Stopped by UDP read loop (one) bridge.Start per datagram bridge.Stop (context cancel, socket close) Datagram handlers the read loop one per datagram, or per session (below) returns; not awaited by Stop TCP accept loop and one reader per connection bridge.Start with Network.TCP per message bridge.Stop ACK pump bridge.Start, when an ACK tracker is attached every 50 ms bridge.Stop Subscription engine tick node.New every 250 ms Node.Stop One report per due subscription the engine tick at most one at a time per subscription returns Session reaper node.New sweep every minute; evicts sessions idle for 5 minutes Node.Stop PASE and CASE handler reapers node.New sweep every minute; evict handlers idle for 30 s Node.Stop Operational-time keeper Node.Start every minute Node.Stop (and waited for) DNS-SD re-announce loop Node.Start, when the advertiser is an mdns.Reannouncer 30 minutes by default Node.Stop Session-triggered re-announce a session event once, bounded by the advertise timeout returns BDX transfer a peer's BDX init on a secure session one per exchange returns Binding manager node.New on change Node.Stop Client stack socket node.New with Config.Client.Enabled per datagram Node.Stop

node.New starts the engine and the reapers before Start. Call Stop on every node New returned, even one you never started.

Every cadence in the table runs on one clock: node.Config.Clock (bridge.Config.Clock for a host that builds the bridge itself), a clock.Clock — the module's one time port, clock.System when unset. No production code outside the clock package reads the time package's clock (clock/noraw_test.go fails the build on one), so a test that passes a clocktest.Fake moves the ACK pump, the engine tick, the reapers, the commissioning window and the cluster timers only when it calls Advance. AfterFunc callbacks run in their own goroutine on either clock. The node's assembler hands the same clock to the Identify server of every bridged endpoint (endpoint.Config.Clock) and to the Aggregator's; a device the host builds with the device layer takes it as device.Options.Clock.

fabrictest runs whole nodes and the module's controller on one clocktest.Fake and an in-memory network, and moves the clock only while no datagram is in flight and no goroutine of the process is working — the Testing in process guide.

Source: transport/udp/listener.go:147-212, bridge/bridge.go:784-840, bridge/ackpump.go:18-24, bridge/ackpump.go:291-314, im/subscription/manager.go:184-185, im/subscription/manager.go:229-235, im/subscription/engine.go:74-95, secure/operational/manager.go:223-227, secure/operational/manager.go:1145-1160, node/security.go:308-355, node/node.go:38-40, node/node.go:486-494, node/reannounce.go:15-31, node/config.go:175-179, bridge/securechannel.go:1268-1290, bridge/bdx_responder.go:93-110, binding/manager.go:238-244, node/client.go:96-106, node/node.go:95-108, clock/clock.go, node/config.go (Config.Clock), endpoint/assembler.go (Config.Clock), node/root.go (buildAggregatorClusters), device/options.go (Options.Clock), fabrictest/site.go (Run).

docs.title: Dispatch and ordering
docs.text:
The read loop copies each datagram and hands it on without blocking.

Messages of one secure unicast session are handled one at a time, in arrival order. The listener keys them by their session id and queues them, so a Read sent right behind an Invoke sees the Invoke's effect. A handler that sends and then waits for the peer's answer on the same session releases its turn first, so the answer is not queued behind it. Examples are a chunked report waiting for its StatusResponse and the subscription priming loop. The TCP transport keeps the same contract per connection.

Everything else runs concurrently: unsecured messages (the PASE and CASE handshakes, session id 0) and group messages. Concurrent unordered handlers are bounded at 1024. A datagram that arrives when every slot is taken is dropped, and the peer's MRP retransmits it. Per session, at most 256 datagrams queue; beyond that a datagram is dropped too.

Between sessions there is no ordering. Two controllers act on the same server concurrently.

Source: bridge/session_order.go:14-69, transport/udp/ordered.go:13-110, transport/udp/listener.go:35-44, transport/udp/listener.go:196-210, transport/tcp/doc.go:24-35.

docs.title: What a host callback may do
docs.text:
The module calls host code from its handler goroutines.

Cluster servers (MatterRead, MatterWrite, MatterInvoke). No dispatcher lock is held while a server is called. A call runs on its session's turn, so a slow MatterInvoke delays that session's next message, and other sessions go on. While it runs, the ACK pump sends a standalone acknowledgement for the request once the standalone-ACK delay (200 ms) has passed, so the controller does not retransmit. Reads also run on the subscription engine's report goroutines, at the same time as commands on other sessions. A server must therefore be safe for concurrent use. The ctx passed to the server ends when the bridge stops.

OnOff's Sink runs with no lock held that Server.Set or a read takes. It may confirm through Set, from its own goroutine or another. Commands, writes and countdown ticks of that server wait behind it.

node.Config.Observers run synchronously on the event's goroutine. For fabric events, that is inside the command that caused the event, before its response is sent, so a blocking observer delays the response. Hand network work to your own goroutine. An observer's error or panic is logged and never returned.

device.Device.OnChanged callbacks run on the server's own change notification. Keep them short. The quickstart only logs.

Controller SubscribeRequest.Updated runs on the goroutine that reads the report, inside the report's exchange. The priming report is delivered inside Subscribe, before it returns. The reference controller hands each report to a channel.

controller/discovery runs one goroutine per Names that holds all cache, service and scanner state. User callbacks never run on that loop.

Source: endpoint/dispatcher.go:364-389, bridge/session_order.go:55-69, bridge/receive.go:185, bridge/ackpump.go:95-105, bridge/ackpump.go:291-295, transport/mrp/ack.go:50-55, node/security.go:308, im/subscription/engine.go:74-95, cluster/onoff/server.go:54-72, cluster/onoff/server.go:749-768, node/observers.go:4-21, device/device.go:643-661, controller/interaction/handler.go:126-138, controller/interaction/subscribe.go:180-200, examples/reference-controller/cli/interact.go:289-330, controller/discovery/doc.go:21-30.

docs.title: Changing the topology
docs.text:
Aggregator.Add and Remove reassemble a running node. Each reassembly takes a fresh snapshot of the set and swaps the new topology in atomically, so an in-flight request always sees one consistent topology.

Two reassemblies that run at the same time are not ordered: the last one to finish wins, even when it took its snapshot first. Call Add, Remove and MarkComplete from one goroutine, or serialise them yourself.

The Snapshotter of a host with its own topology is called at Start and on every Reassemble, and its result is never cached.

Source: node/aggregator.go:70-132, node/aggregator.go:172-178, bridge/bridge.go:868-893, bridge/bridge.go:217-231.

docs.title: Contexts and shutdown
docs.text:
Call Context use node.New takes none. Its goroutines run under the node's lifetime, which Stop cancels Node.Start(ctx) used for the start-up work (assembly, loading the stored fabrics). A cancelled ctx fails Start Node.Run(ctx) starts, waits for ctx to end, then stops with a fresh 5-second budget Node.Stop(ctx) bounds the bridge's wait for its read loop. It closes the sessions with a CloseSession each, stops the engine and reapers, withdraws the mDNS records and closes the advertiser

Stop waits for the read loop, the TCP loop, the ACK pump and the operational-time keeper. It does not wait for datagram handlers that are already running. Their context is cancelled, and a server call can return after Stop has. Close the database only after your own servers have returned, or make them tolerate a closed handle.

Source: node/node.go:109-120, node/node.go:465-535, node/node.go:545-599, bridge/bridge.go:1541-1650, bridge/bridge.go:1805-1812, transport/udp/listener.go:147-212.

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text: A node keeps its state in SQLite. The host opens the database, picks the driver, and owns the handle. The module embeds the DDL its queries are written against, applies it, and never opens a database itself. This page lists what is stored where, what survives a restart, and how schema changes reach a host.

docs.title: Opening the database
docs.text:
db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:node.db?_pragma=foreign_keys(1)&_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)")
  • foreign_keys(1) is required. Removing a fabric deletes its rows through ON DELETE CASCADE, and SQLite ignores foreign keys silently with the pragma off.
  • busy_timeout makes a contended endpoint-number allocation wait instead of failing.
  • Both pragmas go in the DSN. A pragma set with a statement applies to one pooled connection only.

node.New applies the device schemas (store.Apply and sqlitestore.Apply) to Config.Store.DB on every boot. Both scripts are idempotent.

Source: examples/reference-bridge/persist.go:24-60, store/doc.go:8-36, node/node.go:300-317.

docs.title: Tables of store (the matter_* schema)
docs.text: Table Since Holds matter_fabrics v1 (v0.1.0) each fabric: index, fabric id, node id, root certificate and key, vendor, label, compressed fabric id matter_node_identities v1 per fabric: NOC, ICAC, the private key, the IPK as the commissioner sent it matter_group_keys v1 group key sets per fabric, up to three epoch keys matter_group_key_map v1, rebuilt in v3 GroupKeyMap: group id to key set; since v3 without a foreign key, so an entry may name a key set not yet written matter_acl_entries v1 the AccessControl list per fabric, in order matter_resumption v1 CASE resumption records with the peer's CATs matter_diagnostics v1 a single-row counter table with a typed API; the facade keeps its counters in matter_settings instead matter_metadata v1 integer counters: next_fabric_index, event_number_ceiling matter_settings v1 string key/value pairs (next section) matter_persistent_subscriptions v1 unused since v0.3.0; kept so old and new databases have the same schema matter_group_table v2 (v0.2.0) GroupTable: the endpoints of each group matter_groupcast_groups v2 the Groupcast cluster's per-group properties matter_server_subscriptions v2 the subscriptions of active CASE sessions, to re-establish after a restart matter_ota_default_providers v4 (v0.3.0) the OTA requestor's DefaultOTAProviders

docs.text:
Table Holds matter_endpoints one row per source: its stable key's string form, its scope, its endpoint number and device type matter_endpoint_allocation the high-water mark of endpoint numbers. A number is never reused, because a controller caches accessories by number

The stable key's string form is the primary key. If a host changes how its key renders, the row is orphaned and the source gets a new endpoint number.

docs.text:
matter_settings holds the controller-written attribute values and the facade's own state.

Key Written by Holds basic_information.node_label, basic_information.location the facade the root's NodeLabel and Location as a controller wrote them basic_information.configuration_version the facade the root's ConfigurationVersion basic_information.unique_id the facade UniqueID, derived on the first boot and pinned basic_information.unique_id_rotated (deprecated) read once for a migration and cleared bridged_node_label.<key> the facade a bridged endpoint's NodeLabel bridged_configuration_version.<key> the facade a bridged endpoint's ConfigurationVersion scenes.<key> the facade a bridged endpoint's scene table binding.<key>, binding.@<endpoint> the facade an endpoint's Binding list; @ and the number for an endpoint without a stable key user_label.root, user_label.aggregator the facade the UserLabel lists of the root and the Aggregator gendiag.reboot_count the facade RebootCount: 0 on a database's first boot, then one more per boot gendiag.operational_ms the facade accumulated operational time (gendiag.operational_hours is read once as its legacy form) ota_requestor.state store the OTA requestor's state access_control.extension.<fabric> cluster/core AccessControl's Extension list per fabric matter.fabric.<fabric>.vid.statement, .vvsc cluster/core the VID verification statement and VVSC per fabric

Survives Does not survive fabrics, NOCs, keys, ACL live PASE and CASE sessions (controllers reconnect, with resumption) group keys, group table, Groupcast properties the event log's events (their numbers continue past the stored ceiling) endpoint numbers, labels, ConfigurationVersions, scene tables, bindings an open commissioning window (an uncommissioned node opens its own again at Start) CASE resumption records the diagnostic event ring behind DiagnosticLogs the subscriptions of active CASE sessions, re-established under their old ids UniqueID, RebootCount, operational time, OTA default providers

docs.title: The controller database
docs.text:
A controller keeps its state in the same kind of file. The reference controller and the quickstart apply store.Apply (for the settings table) and sqlstore.Apply:

Where Holds matter_settings controller.ca the CA: root certificate, root key, certificate counter (JSON, matter.js field names) matter_settings controller.ca.fabric our fabric: fabric id, root node id, IPK, index, label, our key and NOC matter_settings controller.dcl.trust the DCL trust store (reference controller, with --dcl) matter_client_values each paired node's attribute values, as TLV matter_client_versions each stored cluster's DataVersion

The two controller.ca keys are ca.SettingStore's default; another Key moves both. Controller-side CASE resumption records are kept in memory only, so the first command of a run makes a full CASE handshake.

docs.title: Schema changes
docs.text:
Each schema ships three ways:

  • Apply runs the whole DDL. It is idempotent and safe on every boot. store.Apply then runs store.Upgrade, which rebuilds what an idempotent CREATE cannot change (the v3 rebuild of matter_group_key_map).
  • Migrations() returns the same schema as versioned steps (v1, v2, …), each with Up and Down, for a host that runs its own migration tool. A released step never changes. Pin len(Migrations()) and the last version, so the next release's new step fails the pin at the dependency bump instead of at a live write. v3's Down is lossy.
  • SchemaFingerprint(db) hashes the module's tables and indexes as SQLite records them. Compare it with the value the CHANGELOG records for the release to know your tables match. A host's own tables and indexes do not change it.
Package Schema/Apply Migrations SchemaFingerprint store yes yes yes controller/client/sqlstore yes yes (its own list) yes endpoint/sqlitestore yes no no

The schemas are independent and can be applied in either order.

Source: store/schema.go:23-90, store/migrations.go:22-120, controller/client/sqlstore/sqlstore.go:11-16, controller/client/sqlstore/schema.go:31-104, endpoint/sqlitestore/sqlitestore.go:68-72, endpoint/sqlitestore/schema.sql:8-11.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
The module ships no backup tool. What a backup has to respect:

  • The file holds private keys. The node's operational keys and the controller's CA key are stored unencrypted. The store's documentation leaves file-system protection to the operator. Protect the database and every copy of it like the keys.
  • Copy a consistent state. Stop the node first, or use SQLite's own online mechanisms (VACUUM INTO, the backup API). Copying the file of a running node can catch a write half-done.
  • Run one copy at a time. A restored database is the same node: the same fabrics, the same operational identity. Two running copies answer as one node under one identity.

Source: store/doc.go:38-40, store/schema.sql:48-57, examples/reference-controller/README.md (The database).

docs.title: Host ports
docs.text:
A host reaches the module through ports: interfaces it implements, configuration fields it fills, and calls that attach a collaborator. This page lists them by where they live. For each port it says what the port does and what happens when you leave it out.

Two failure modes recur, and they are not interchangeable:

  • Fails closed: the request is refused. A controller at least sees a denial.
  • Silent: the reply looks well-formed, and the missing behaviour never shows up as an error anywhere.

Source: bridge/bridge.go:38-47.

docs.title: contract/: what a device and a server implement
docs.text: contract/ imports the standard library only. A host type that implements these interfaces does not drag the host's dependencies into the module.

docs.title: bridge: the Attach… and Set… ports
docs.text: The facade attaches all of these. A host that drives bridge/ directly attaches them itself, in this order. bridge.New installs a no-op for each port that is not attached.

docs.title: Before Start
docs.text:
These are read once at Start, or feed a component Start builds.

Port Failure mode What a skip costs AttachACLLister fails closed every fabric-scoped request is denied with UnsupportedAccess. endpoint.UnenforcedACL is the explicit way to run without an ACL AttachSessionLookup silent every encrypted datagram is dropped. CASE completes and carries no traffic AttachPaseHandlerProvider (or AttachPaseHandler) fails closed commissioning cannot begin. Prefer the provider: the singleton serialises commissioners AttachCaseHandlerProvider (or AttachCaseHandler) fails closed no CASE. A singleton rejects the parallel CASE sessions Apple Home opens AttachAckTracker silent no standalone ACKs and no retransmission of the bridge's own messages; every reply is best-effort. It wraps the lower-level AttachAckHandler AttachSubscriptionManager silent a Subscribe returns its initial report with no subscription id, and no report follows AttachSessionRegistry silent CloseSession closes nothing, Stop sends no farewell, and the re-announce trigger is not installed AttachSubscriptionStore silent nothing survives a restart; controllers wait out their liveness timeout. SetSubscriptionPersistence(false) switches persistence off on purpose

docs.title: Cluster surface
docs.text:
Attaching republishes onto the live topology immediately, as well as on the next Reassemble.

Port Failure mode What a skip costs AttachRootClusters, then AttachAggregatorClusters silent for wildcards a wildcard read skips the empty endpoint, so the bridge looks present and empty AttachRootPartsListProvider, AttachAggregatorPartsListProvider silent must follow their cluster call. They return false when no Descriptor is mounted, and PartsList stays frozen
